chapters.title: Faith under persecution and righteous judgment

parts.text: Paul thanks God for the Thessalonians’ growing faith and increasing love, boasting of their perseverance amid persecution. Their endurance points to God’s righteous judgment and their calling to his kingdom. God will repay affliction to their oppressors and give the afflicted rest when Jesus is revealed from heaven with mighty angels. Those who do not know God or obey the gospel face everlasting destruction, while Christ is glorified and admired among those who believe.

Paul continually prays that God will count them worthy of his calling and powerfully fulfil their good desires and work of faith. His desire is that the name of Jesus Christ be glorified in them and they in him, according to God’s grace. Their present trials are thus set alongside God’s final justice and the faithful life he enables now.

chapters.title: The man of sin and steadfast faith

parts.text: Paul warns against messages or purported letters claiming that the day of Christ is at hand. A falling away and revelation of the man of sin must first occur. This opponent exalts himself in God’s temple, claiming divine status. Iniquity already works, but restraint remains until the restrainer is removed; then the wicked one is revealed and destroyed by the Lord’s coming. His satanic signs deceive those who reject the truth, and God gives them over to delusion and judgment.

In contrast, Paul thanks God for believers chosen to salvation through the Spirit’s sanctification and belief in the truth, called through the gospel to share Christ’s glory. They must stand firm in the teaching received orally and by letter. Paul asks Jesus Christ and the Father, who have given lasting comfort and good hope through grace, to strengthen their hearts in every good word and work.

Paul asks for prayer that the Lord’s word spread freely and be honoured, and that the missionaries be delivered from wicked people. Although not everyone has faith, the Lord is faithful and will strengthen and guard the believers. Paul expresses confidence in their obedience and prays that their hearts be directed into God’s love and patient waiting for Christ.

Believers must withdraw from brothers living disorderly contrary to apostolic instruction. Paul reminds them that he worked tirelessly to avoid burdening anyone and to give an example, teaching that anyone unwilling to work should not eat. Busybody idleness must give way to quiet work and self-support. The church should persist in doing good and correct disobedient members without treating them as enemies. Paul closes with a prayer for peace and his own handwritten greeting authenticating the letter.
